chapter_outcomes: understand the assessment objectives: AO1 - Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of science, AO2(a) - Application of knowledge and understanding of science in familiar and unfamiliar contexts, AO2(b) - Analysis and evaluation of scientific information to make judgments and reach conclusions, AO3 - Experimental skills in science, including analysis and evaluation of data and methods
understand the structure of written examinations: multiple-choice, short-open, open-response, calculations and extended-writing questions
understand that papers will include a minimum of 8-10% marks that target mathematics at Level 2 or above
understand that candidates will be expected to apply their knowledge and understanding to familiar and unfamiliar contexts
understand that Unit 5 paper includes pre-released reading (scientific article) underpinning one question carrying 20 marks
understand that papers may include synoptic questions which require knowledge and understanding from multiple units
be able to use calculators appropriately in examinations

understand the use of command words in examinations: Add/Label, Assess, Calculate, Comment on, Compare and contrast, Complete/Record, Criticise, Deduce, Derive, Describe, Determine, Devise, Discuss, Draw, Estimate, Evaluate, Explain, Give/State/Name, Give a reason/reasons, Identify, Justify, Plot, Predict, Show that, Sketch, State what is meant by, Suggest, Write
